The-Gleaming-Coil.title: The Gleaming Coil
The-Gleaming-Coil.content:
The Gleaming Coil - Shop in the Radiant Citadel Trade Discal
Purveyor of Expeditionary Necessities & Arcane Curiosities
Located in the bustling Trade Disc of the Radiant Citadel, nestled between a perfume merchant and a cartographer’s studio

The Shop
The Gleaming Coil occupies a narrow but deep storefront with polished brass fixtures and warm amber lighting from enchanted lanterns. The proprietor, Merchant Kalista Voh, is a half-elf woman in her fifties who wears reading spectacles on a chain and keeps meticulous ledgers. She’s traveled to most of the Concord civilizations and has an eye for quality gear.
The shop smells of leather oil, parchment, and a faint metallic tang from the magical items kept in warded cases. Kalista is professional, fair, and happy to haggle—but only if customers demonstrate genuine knowledge of what they’re buying (DC 13 Persuasion check for 10% discount, DC 18 for 15%).

Standard Adventuring Gear
All items at normal PHB prices unless noted
Weapons & Armor (made to order, 2-day wait):

Any non-magical weapon from PHB
Any non-magical armor from PHB
Silvered weapons (+100 gp)
Adamantine weapons (if applicable, +500 gp)

Adventuring Equipment (in stock):

Complete Explorer’s Pack, Burglar’s Pack, Dungeoneer’s Pack, Priest’s Pack, Scholar’s Pack (PHB prices)
Climber’s Kit, Healer’s Kit, Herbalism Kit, Poisoner’s Kit (PHB prices)
Holy Water (25 gp per vial) — Kalista keeps various faiths in stock
Antitoxin (50 gp)
Oil of Slipperiness (as flask, non-magical, 15 gp) — makes surfaces slick
Quality Rope, Silk (10 gp per 50 ft.) — lighter and stronger than hemp
Spyglass (1,000 gp)
Magnifying Glass (100 gp)


Magical Items for Sale
Kalista keeps these behind enchanted glass. She’ll let customers handle them but watches carefully.

Common Magic Items (100 gp each)
Candle of the Deep (×3 available) A candle that burns underwater and creates a 5-foot radius sphere of bright light and another 5 feet of dim light. Burns for 1 hour per lighting.
Cloak of Billowing This cloak billows dramatically at your mental command. Pure style, no mechanical benefit.
Orb of Direction A fist-sized glass sphere with a golden needle. While held, you always know which way is north.
Pipe of Smoke Monsters (×2 available) Smoke exhaled from this pipe takes whimsical shapes—dragons, ships, faces—at your mental command.

Uncommon Magic Items
Boots of Elvenkind — 2,500 gp Your footsteps make no sound. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that rely on moving silently.
Cloak of Protection — 3,500 gp While wearing this cloak, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws.
Goggles of Night — 1,800 gp While wearing these dark lenses, you have Darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, wearing the goggles increases its range by 60 feet.
Sending Stones (pair) — 2,000 gp Smooth river stones carved with matching runes. Once per day, a creature holding one can cast Sending to communicate with whoever holds the other stone.
Weapon +1 (your choice) — 1,500 gp Kalista has a +1 longsword, +1 shortbow, and +1 quarterstaff currently in stock. She can order other weapon types (1 week delivery, 200 gp surcharge).
Bag of Holding — 4,000 gp (only 1 available) The classic. Holds 500 pounds in a 64-cubic-foot space. Weighs 15 pounds regardless of contents.
Eversmoking Bottle — 1,200 gp Uncork this brass bottle to produce a 60-foot-radius cloud of thick smoke that spreads around corners. The cloud persists for 1 minute or until a strong wind disperses it. One use per day.
Eyes of Charming — 3,000 gp These crystal lenses fit over your eyes. You can use an action to cast Charm Person (save DC 13). Once used three times, the eyes can’t be used again until the next dawn.
Pearl of Power — 6,000 gp Once per day while holding this pearl, you can use a Bonus Action to regain one expended spell slot of 3rd level or lower.
Slippers of Spider Climbing — 2,800 gp While you wear these light shoes, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings, while leaving your hands free. You have a Climbing Speed equal to your walking speed.

Rare Magic Items (Special Order)
Kalista has contacts in several Concord civilizations who can acquire rarer items. Delivery takes 2-4 weeks and requires a 25% deposit.
Weapon +2 — 8,000 gp
Armor +1 — 6,000 gp (depends on base armor type)
Ring of Evasion — 12,000 gp Three charges. When you fail a Dexterity saving throw, you can use your Reaction to expend 1 charge and succeed instead. Recharges 1d3 charges daily at dawn.
Necklace of Prayer Beads — 10,000 gp (requires divine spellcaster) Contains 1d4+2 magic beads that cast spells like Bless, Cure Wounds, or Greater Restoration.

Potions & Consumables
Kept in a temperature-controlled cabinet with labels in multiple languages.
Potion of Healing — 50 gp (unlimited stock) Restores 2d4+2 hit points.
Potion of Greater Healing — 250 gp (×6 available) Restores 4d4+4 hit points.
Potion of Climbing — 75 gp (×4 available) Gain a Climbing Speed equal to your walking speed for 1 hour.
Potion of Water Breathing — 180 gp (×3 available) You can breathe underwater for 1 hour.
Potion of Resistance (specify type) — 300 gp (×2 each of Fire, Cold, Lightning) Gain resistance to one damage type for 1 hour.
Oil of Sharpness — 1,600 gp (×1 available) Apply to a weapon (takes 1 minute). For 1 hour, that weapon becomes a +3 magic weapon.
Potion of Invisibility — 500 gp (×2 available) You become Invisible for 1 hour or until you attack or cast a spell.
Elixir of Health — 250 gp (×3 available) Cures any disease and removes the Poisoned condition.

Services
Identification — 25 gp per item Kalista can cast Identify (she has a pearl worth 100 gp for the material component). Takes 10 minutes.
Appraisal — 10 gp She’ll assess the value of gems, art objects, or trade goods.
Armor Fitting — 50 gp Ensures armor fits perfectly, removing any Disadvantage on Stealth from poor fit (within reason).

Additional Specialized Items at The Gleaming Coil
Kalista notices the party’s composition and gestures toward some items she keeps for “specialists.”

For the Warlock
Uncommon Items
Rod of the Pact Keeper +1 — 3,500 gp While holding this slender obsidian rod, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your warlock spells. In addition, you can regain one expended Pact Magic spell slot as an action while holding the rod. Once used, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.
Kalista’s note: “Pact rods attune to the wielder’s patron. This one hums slightly—I believe it last served a Fiend warlock, but it will adapt.”
Eldritch Claw Tattoo — 2,800 gp (Uncommon, requires attunement) This tattoo appears as eldritch symbols across your hand and forearm. While attuned, your unarmed strikes are considered magical and deal 1d6 Force damage. As a Bonus Action, you can empower the tattoo for 1 minute (recharge on a Long Rest), during which your unarmed strikes deal an extra 1d6 Force damage and have a reach of 15 feet (spectral claws extend from your hands).
Kalista’s note: “Popular with Hexblades and those who prefer close combat. Application takes about an hour—I work with a tattoo artist two streets over.”
Tome of Ancient Secrets (Empty) — 500 gp A leather-bound book with blank vellum pages and a lock of braided silver hair as a bookmark. Perfect for a Pact of the Tome warlock to inscribe ritual spells. The pages resist water, fire, and aging. Contains enough pages for 20 spells.
Eldritch Focusing Crystal — 800 gp This purple-black crystal on a chain serves as both an arcane focus and has 3 charges. When you cast Eldritch Blast, you can expend 1 charge as part of the same action to add 1d8 Force damage to one beam. Regains 1d3 charges at dawn.

For the Cleric
Uncommon Items
Amulet of the Devout +1 — 3,500 gp This holy symbol bears the mark of a deity (Kalista can arrange for any deity in the Concord civilizations). While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your cleric spells. You can use a Bonus Action to expend one use of your Channel Divinity to regain one expended spell slot of a level no higher than half your proficiency bonus (rounded up). Once used, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.
Kalista’s note: “I can have this consecrated to your specific deity. Give me a day and 50 gp for the ritual components.”
Periapt of Wound Closure — 2,500 gp While wearing this pendant, you stabilize whenever you’re dying at the start of your turn. In addition, whenever you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, you regain the maximum number of hit points possible for that die (for example, rolling a d8 would automatically restore 8 hit points plus your Constitution modifier).
Kalista’s note: “Essential for battlefield healers. I’ve seen this save lives when the cleric themselves goes down.”
Prayer Wheel of Sanctuary — 1,200 gp This small bronze wheel inscribed with prayers can be spun as a Bonus Action. When spun, it casts Sanctuary on you (save DC 13) without requiring Concentration. Once used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.
Censer of Controlling Air Elementals — 4,500 gp (Rare) While burning incense in this vessel (10 gp worth), you can use an action to cast Conjure Elemental to summon an air elemental. The censer can’t be used this way again until the next dawn.
Kalista’s note: “Popular with clerics of storm or sky deities. The incense lasts 1 hour per use.”
Sacred Candles (Consumable) — 20 gp per set of 4 When lit during a ceremony spell or while casting healing spells, these candles add 1d4 to the result. Each candle burns for 1 hour. They smell of frankincense and myrrh.

For the Goliath Barbarian
Uncommon Items
Belt of Giant Strength (Hill Giant) — 7,500 gp (Rare) While wearing this belt, your Strength score becomes 21 (unless it’s already higher). The belt is made from the hide of a hill giant and fitted with an iron buckle.
Kalista’s note: “I have only the Hill Giant variant in stock. I could order Stone Giant or Frost Giant versions, but those run 15,000-25,000 gp and take a month.”
Bracers of Defense — 3,000 gp While wearing these bracers and not wearing armor or wielding a shield, you gain a +2 bonus to AC.
Kalista’s note: “Perfect for unarmored fighters. These are ironwood carved with mountain runes—very Goliath aesthetic.”
Javelin of Lightning — 1,800 gp This javelin is a magic weapon. When you throw it and speak its command word, it transforms into a bolt of lightning. Make a ranged weapon attack (normal range 120 feet). On a hit, the target takes 4d6 Lightning damage instead of normal damage. All creatures within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 4d6 Lightning damage (half on success). The javelin then returns to its normal form in your hand or at your feet if you have no hand free.
Kalista’s note: “Throwing weapon that comes back. What barbarian doesn’t want that?”
Periapt of Health — 2,200 gp You are immune to contracting any disease while wearing this pendant. If you are already diseased when you don it, the pendant suppresses the disease (but doesn’t cure it).
Kalista’s note: “Adventurers who charge into swamps, sewers, and plague zones swear by these.”
Horn of Valhalla (Brass) — 6,000 gp (Rare) You can use an action to blow this horn. In response, 2d4+2 berserker spirits from the plane of Ysgard appear within 60 feet of you. They use the Berserker stat block and return to Ysgard after 1 hour or when they drop to 0 hit points. Once used, the horn can’t be used again until 7 days have passed.
Kalista’s note: “Your ancestors answer when you call. Very on-brand for Goliath culture.”
Stone of Goliath Endurance — 1,500 gp (custom item) This smooth gray stone is carved with the markings of various Goliath clans. Once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can drop to 1 hit point instead and gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus.
Kalista’s note: “I commissioned this from a Goliath stone-singer. Embodies the ‘stones endure’ philosophy.”

For the Rogue
Uncommon Items
Cloak of Elvenkind — 3,000 gp While wearing this cloak with its hood up, you have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and Wisdom (Perception) checks made to see you have Disadvantage.
Kalista’s note: “The classic. Combines well with those Boots of Elvenkind I showed you earlier—total stealth package.”
Gloves of Thievery — 2,500 gp These gloves are invisible while worn. While wearing them, you gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and Dexterity checks made to pick locks.
Kalista’s note: “No judgment here. I assume you’re recovering stolen property.”
Shadow Blade Oil — 400 gp per vial (×3 available, consumable) When applied to a weapon (takes 1 action), that weapon deals an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage on its next hit and emits no sound when it strikes. The effect lasts for 1 minute or until the weapon hits.
Ring of Mind Shielding — 3,500 gp While wearing this ring, you are immune to magic that allows creatures to read your thoughts, determine if you’re lying, know your alignment, or know your creature type. Thoughts can only be read if you allow it. If you die while wearing the ring, your soul enters it (unless it already houses a soul). You can remain in the ring or depart for the afterlife. While in the ring, you can communicate telepathically with any creature wearing it.
Kalista’s note: “Popular with spies, informants, and anyone who keeps secrets for a living.”
Slippers of Spider Climbing — 2,800 gp (Listed above but especially relevant for rogues)
Boots of Speed — 4,000 gp (Rare) While wearing these boots, you can use a Bonus Action and click the heels together to double your walking speed and make Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage. The effect lasts for 10 minutes. The boots have 4 charges and regain 1d4 charges daily at dawn.
Kalista’s note: “Get in, get the goods, get out. Fast.”
Dagger of Venom — 2,500 gp This dagger is a +1 weapon. You can use an action to cause thick, black poison to coat the blade. The poison remains for 1 minute or until an attack using this weapon hits a creature. That creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 2d10 Poison damage and become Poisoned for 1 minute. The dagger can’t be used this way again until the next dawn.
Rope of Entanglement — 3,200 gp (Rare) This 30-foot length of silk rope weighs 3 pounds. You can use an action to speak its command word and throw it at a creature you can see within 20 feet. Make a ranged attack roll (Dexterity + proficiency). On a hit, the target is Restrained. The rope has AC 20, 20 hit points, and immunity to Psychic and Poison damage. The rope can be used this way once per day.
Kalista’s note: “Nonlethal takedowns. Very professional.”
Dust of Disappearance — 300 gp per pouch (×2 available, consumable) When thrown into the air (action), this dust makes you and each creature and object within 10 feet of you Invisible for 2d4 minutes. The invisibility ends for a creature when it attacks or casts a spell.

Additional Services for Specialists
Poison & Antidote Consultation — 50 gp + cost of materials Kalista keeps a reference book on toxins. She can advise on poisons (for rogues), acquire legal toxins, or provide custom antitoxins. Basic Poison (100 gp), Purple Worm Poison (special order, 2,000 gp).
Warlock Pact Research — 100 gp Kalista has traveled extensively and knows scholars of the arcane. She can provide information about potential patrons, pact marks, or connect warlocks with others who share their patron type.
Holy Symbol Consecration — 50 gp + 1 day For clerics, Kalista works with various temple representatives in the Citadel to properly consecrate holy symbols to specific deities.
Climbing Gear Package — 150 gp Includes: climber’s kit, 100 ft. silk rope, grappling hook, pitons (20), and chalk. Kalista’s note: “Goliaths climb instinctively, but even you might need backup.”

Kalista’s Special Offer
She leans in conspiratorially:
“I can tell you’re a capable group. If you’re interested in a Group Discount, I’m willing to offer 10% off your total purchase if it exceeds 5,000 gp. I value repeat customers, especially ones who survive their adventures and come back with interesting stories—and perhaps items to sell.”

index.content:
Andrew Plemmons Pratt here. I am an experienced human-centered designer, educator, curriculum developer, and program builder. I weave together innovation methods and race equity tools to transform civic institutions and systems through rigorous learning.
Most recently, I worked at The Lab @ OPM. This human-centered design shop in the U.S. Office of Personnel Management builds capacity for government organizations to transform their programs and processes by teaching human-centered design and partnering with federal agencies on complex civic challenges. While there I did things like:

Led human-centered design courses for 350+ civil servants at agencies across state and federal governments
Led the redesign and delivery of our immersive, multi-week flagship Civic Design Studio course
Wrote a new course on human-centered design fundamentals for civil servants
Coached federal leaders on implementation of food and nutrition assistance rules, service design for human resources programs, and processes for managing ethics obligations for government employees
Conducted prototype testing and synthesis with participants to refine a co-designed Trauma-Informed Disaster Recovery Training Program for FEMA emergency responders

Before working as a civil servant, I built and led equity-centered education innovation programs at CityBridge Education.
Check out my full portfolio of civic design and school innovation work here.
I also bake bread, learn to play piano, relish tabletop games, volunteer at my kids’ DC public school, and make things out of fabric, wood, and bits.
Some things I’ve written:
Serious Games and Design: Games can serve as tools for analyzing systems. First draft.
Designing for Race Equity: Now Is the Time
Segregation, Assimilation, and Anti-Racism in Ibram Kendi’s “Stamped from the Beginning”
Computers as Objects to Think With + on Goodreads
